title: api: unify rate-limit/retry semantics, idempotency, and streaming error surface for OpenAI-compatibility
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: In the OpenAI-compatibility layer we had several inconsistencies in how rate-limits, idempotency, and mid-stream errors were surfaced to clients. Different endpoints returned slightly different 429 payloads, Retry-After headers were sometimes omitted or expressed in ms, and streaming endpoints did not always emit a terminal error event when upstream failures occurred mid-stream. This caused surprising client-side behavior in our SDKs and customer integrations (duplicated requests, unclear retry guidance, and broken streaming consumers).

This PR: unifies rate-limit and retry semantics across REST and streaming endpoints, standardizes idempotency-key handling (including streaming/function-calling use cases), and provides a consistent OpenAI-compatible error surface and mapping. Key user-visible changes: consistent error.code values (rate_limit, idempotency_conflict, server_error), Retry-After communicated via both HTTP header (seconds) and JSON body field (retry_after_seconds) where applicable, idempotency conflict returns 409 with an explanatory body, streaming endpoints emit a final structured error event before closing the stream.

Why now: Several incidents and SDK bug reports highlighted this gap (SUP-712), and the inconsistency blocks safe client-side retry strategies for our hosted API and Private deployments. This change reduces customer surprises and makes SDK-level retry logic deterministic.

Checklist:
- [x] Spec: document rate-limit/body/header semantics and error.code mapping
- [x] Implementation: server-side handlers and streaming manager changes
- [x] OpenAI compatibility layer mapping tests
- [x] End-to-end streaming tests (simulate upstream 5xx mid-stream)
- [x] SDK tests adjusted for new idempotency conflict behavior
- [x] Docs: docs/openai-compat/errors.md updated

Notes: This is intentionally conservative on semantics (seconds for Retry-After) to match common HTTP client expectations and to align with OpenAI compat. No behavioural change to existing idempotency dedupe window (48 hours) but the API surface clarifies response shape for duplicates and conflicts.

c2a7d89: api: normalize 429 payload and add retry_after_seconds to body
e14f0ab: streaming: emit terminal error event and ensure event ordering
f3b2c57: idempotency: dedupe key check + 409 conflict response for duplicates
d9a7bd4: openai-compat: map internal errors -> openai error codes and messages
a6e1c3d: tests: add integration/e2e streaming failure scenarios
9c8f2b1: docs: document error schema in docs/openai-compat/errors.md
review_comments:
Ethan Park: Nice spec. A couple things: 1) confirm Retry-After header is always seconds (not ms) and we should add a small note about clocks skew for private deployments. 2) for streaming, what does SDK do if the client already consumed partial events?

Aisha Kapoor (author): We're returning seconds in the Retry-After header and the JSON field retry_after_seconds to avoid ambiguity. We'll add a note about clock skew to the docs. For SDKs we added a deterministic terminal error event (event.type="error") so consumers always see a final structured signal before the stream closes. SDKs can treat that the same as a non-streaming 4xx/5xx error for retry logic.

Sofia Martinez: Implementation detail: is idempotency dedupe performed synchronously against the same store used by Dedicated/Private? Concern about contention and latency.

Aisha Kapoor (author): We're reusing the existing idempotency store with a short local cache in front for reads to avoid extra round trips on hot paths. The store remains the source of truth and the dedupe logic is amortized; added metrics to monitor contention (idempotency.store.hits/misses/lock_latency).

Rahul Iyer: Tests look good. Did you consider returning 429 vs 503 for overload vs transient upstream errors mid-stream? We currently return server_error for upstream 5xx and rate_limit for throttles.

Aisha Kapoor (author): We keep 429 for explicit throttling enforced by our quota/rate limiter. For upstream transient failures that manifest mid-stream we return a server_error with HTTP 502/503 (depending on upstream), plus a structured error event in the stream and include Retry-After when we think backoff is appropriate.
release_notes: Unify rate-limit and retry semantics across REST and streaming endpoints; standardize idempotency conflict responses; streaming endpoints now emit a terminal structured error event on upstream failures; OpenAI-compat layer maps internal errors to consistent error.code values (rate_limit, idempotency_conflict, server_error). Refer to docs/openai-compat/errors.md for full schema and migration notes.
notes_for_ops: Monitor idempotency.store.lock_latency and idempotency.conflict_rate after rollout
Watch for increased 429s from dedicated pools during ramp; the Retry-After header is expressed in seconds
Audit SDKs for handling of terminal streaming error events (event.type="error")
